coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Hexadecimal and decimal: equal or not
coding.question: You are given two numbers as text: H, written in hexadecimal (base 16, digits 0-9 and letters A-F in upper or lower case), and D, written in decimal. Print EQUAL if they have the same value, otherwise print NOT EQUAL. If H is not a valid hexadecimal number or D is not a valid decimal number, print INVALID instead. A valid number has only allowed digits: no sign, no spaces, no prefix like 0x.
coding.input_format:
Line 1: the text H.
Line 2: the text D.
coding.output_format: One line: EQUAL, NOT EQUAL or INVALID.
coding.constraints:
1 <= length of H <= 15
1 <= length of D <= 18
H and D have no spaces.
coding.starter_code:
h = input().strip()
d = input().strip()
# TODO: write your logic here
print("INVALID")
hints: Check every character first; only convert when both texts are valid.
int(h, 16) converts hexadecimal text in Python, but it also accepts a 0x prefix, so validate yourself.
coding.explanation: Validate H against the hex digits and D against 0-9, then convert H with base 16 and D with base 10 and compare. Time O(length).
coding.label: Candidate-reported

coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Extract numbers and shorten three trailing zeros
coding.question: A string S contains letters, digits and symbols. A number is a maximal group of consecutive digits. Print every number in the order it appears. If a number ends with three zeros, replace those last three zeros with a single zero (so 1000 becomes 10 and 25000 becomes 250). Print other numbers exactly as they appear. If S has no digits, print -1.
coding.input_format: One line: the string S (no spaces).
coding.output_format: One line: the numbers separated by single spaces, or -1.
coding.starter_code:
s = input().strip()
# TODO: write your logic here
print(-1)
hints: Collect digits into a current number and close it when a non-digit appears.
Work with the numbers as text so leading zeros are kept.
coding.explanation: Scan the string once, building each run of digits; when a run ends, apply the three-zeros rule and store it. Adding a sentinel character at the end closes the last run. Time O(n).
coding.label: Candidate-reported

coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Valid password checker
coding.question: A password is valid when all of these are true: it has at least 8 characters, at least one uppercase letter (A-Z), at least one lowercase letter (a-z), at least one digit (0-9) and at least one special character (any character that is not a letter or a digit, like @ # $ !). Check the given password.
coding.input_format: One line: the password P (no spaces).
coding.constraints:
1 <= length of P <= 100
P has printable ASCII characters and no spaces.
coding.starter_code:
p = input().strip()
# TODO: write your logic here
print("Invalid")
coding.solution:
p = input().strip()
up = any('A' <= c <= 'Z' for c in p)
lo = any('a' <= c <= 'z' for c in p)
dg = any('0' <= c <= '9' for c in p)
sp = any(not ('A' <= c <= 'Z' or 'a' <= c <= 'z' or '0' <= c <= '9') for c in p)
print("Valid" if len(p) >= 8 and up and lo and dg and sp else "Invalid")
hints: Use four flags (upper, lower, digit, special) and set them in one pass.
coding.explanation: One pass over the password sets a flag for each character type; the password is valid when the length is at least 8 and all four flags are true. Time O(n).
coding.label: Candidate-reported

coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: LCM of two numbers
coding.question: Given two positive integers A and B, print their LCM (least common multiple), the smallest positive number divisible by both.
coding.input_format: One line: two integers A and B.
coding.starter_code:
a, b = map(int, input().split())
# TODO: write your logic here
print(a * b)
coding.solution:
a, b = map(int, input().split())
x, y = a, b
while y:
    x, y = y, x % y
print(a // x * b)
hints: LCM(a, b) = a * b / GCD(a, b).
Find the GCD with Euclid's method: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b).
coding.explanation: Compute the GCD with the Euclidean algorithm, then LCM = a / gcd * b (dividing first keeps the numbers small). Time O(log min(a, b)).
coding.label: Candidate-reported

coding.title: Decimal to binary, octal and hexadecimal
coding.question: Given a non-negative decimal integer N, print it in binary (base 2), octal (base 8) and hexadecimal (base 16). Do not print any prefix such as 0b, 0o or 0x, and use capital letters A-F for hexadecimal.
coding.output_format:
Line 1: N in binary.
Line 2: N in octal.
Line 3: N in hexadecimal.
coding.starter_code:
n = int(input())
# TODO: write your logic here
print(n)
hints: Repeatedly divide by the base and collect the remainders, then reverse them.
Remember that N = 0 should print 0 on every line.
coding.explanation: Repeated division by the base gives the digits from last to first; reverse them. Python's format(n, 'b'), 'o' and 'X' do the same. Time O(log N).

coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Sort by number of 1 bits
coding.question: Given N non-negative integers, sort them by the number of 1s in their binary form, from fewest to most. If two numbers have the same count of 1 bits, the smaller number comes first.
coding.input_format:
Line 1: integer N.
Line 2: N non-negative integers.
coding.output_format: One line: the sorted numbers separated by single spaces.
coding.starter_code:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
# TODO: write your logic here
print(" ".join(map(str, a)))
coding.solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
a.sort(key=lambda x: (bin(x).count("1"), x))
print(" ".join(map(str, a)))
hints: bin(x).count('1') gives the number of 1 bits in Python.
Sort with the key (bit count, value).
coding.explanation: Sort with a two-part key: the number of set bits, then the value itself. Counting bits is O(log V) per number, so the total is O(n log n).
coding.label: AI practice
coding.source_note: Written for practice on IBM's reported coding topics

coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Add two binary numbers
coding.question: Given two binary numbers as strings, print their sum as a binary string. Do not print leading zeros (the sum 0 is printed as 0).
coding.input_format:
Line 1: binary string A.
Line 2: binary string B.
coding.output_format: One line: A + B in binary.
coding.constraints:
1 <= length of A, B <= 1000
A and B contain only 0 and 1 and have no leading zeros (except the number 0 itself).
coding.starter_code:
a = input().strip()
b = input().strip()
# TODO: add from the right, keeping a carry
print(0)
coding.solution:
a = input().strip()
b = input().strip()
i, j, carry, out = len(a) - 1, len(b) - 1, 0, []
while i >= 0 or j >= 0 or carry:
    s = carry
    if i >= 0:
        s += int(a[i]); i -= 1
    if j >= 0:
        s += int(b[j]); j -= 1
    out.append(str(s % 2))
    carry = s // 2
res = "".join(reversed(out)).lstrip("0")
print(res if res else "0")
hints: Work from the last character of both strings, like adding on paper.
In base 2, digit = sum % 2 and carry = sum // 2.
coding.explanation: Walk both strings from the right, adding digits and the carry; append sum % 2 and carry sum // 2. Reverse at the end and strip leading zeros. O(len(A) + len(B)). (In Python, bin(int(a, 2) + int(b, 2))[2:] also works, but interviewers expect the manual method.)
coding.label: AI practice
coding.source_note: Written for practice on IBM's reported coding topics

coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Minimum ship capacity in D days
coding.question: N packages must be shipped in the given order, and package i weighs w[i]. Each day the ship is loaded with packages in order (you cannot skip or reorder) as long as the total weight does not go over the ship's capacity. Find the smallest capacity that lets all packages be shipped within D days.
coding.input_format:
Line 1: two integers N and D.
Line 2: N integers, the weights in order.
coding.starter_code:
n, d = map(int, input().split())
w = list(map(int, input().split()))
# TODO: write your logic here
print(sum(w))
hints: The answer lies between the heaviest package and the total weight.
For a fixed capacity you can count the days greedily; if it fits in D days, try a smaller capacity.
coding.explanation: Binary search the capacity between max(w) and sum(w). For each candidate, load packages greedily and count days; feasibility only gets easier as capacity grows. Time O(n log(sum(w))).
coding.label: AI practice
coding.source_note: Written for practice on IBM's reported coding topics

coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Longest subarray with equal 0s and 1s
coding.question: Given a binary array (every value is 0 or 1), find the length of the longest subarray (continuous part) that has the same number of 0s and 1s. If there is no such subarray, print 0.
coding.input_format:
Line 1: integer N.
Line 2: N values, each 0 or 1.
coding.starter_code:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
# TODO: write your logic here
print(0)
hints: Treat 0 as -1; then you need the longest subarray with sum 0.
Remember the first index where each prefix sum appeared.
coding.explanation: Replace 0 with -1 and keep a running sum. Two equal prefix sums mean the part between them has equal 0s and 1s, so store the first index of each sum and measure the distance. Time O(n).

mcq.question: What number does this query return?

Table students:          Table marks:
| id | name  |             | student_id | score |
| 1  | Asha  |             | 1          | 80    |
| 2  | Ravi  |             | 1          | 75    |
| 3  | Meena |             | 3          | 90    |
| 4  | John  |

SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM students s
LEFT JOIN marks m ON s.id = m.student_id;
mcq.explanation: Asha matches 2 rows, Meena 1, and Ravi and John have no marks but are kept with NULLs: 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 5.
